fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the street entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so emergency apparatus can reach the property without obstruction.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the detached structure or open lawn area so fire and emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing long distances down the driveway.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so it does not narrow the travel width or obstruct the roofline clearance for larger vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation that grows directly against or overhangs the main residence so responders can move along the exterior walls during operations.
• Cut back dense vegetation that grows directly against or overhangs the detached structure for the same reason.
• Thin dense vegetation between the street and the structures so responders approaching on foot have a clear line of sight to both buildings.
• Keep a gate, if present at the single access point, unlocked or equipped with a Knox-type lock box so responders are not delayed at the entry.
• Post a site map or property diagram at the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence, detached structure, and access drive to orient

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure on all sides.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure so branches do not hang close to the ground or roofline.
• Clear brush from the area surrounding the structure to open up space between vegetation and the building.
• Separate shrubs and trees near the structure so they do not connect to each other in a continuous line leading toward the building.
• Cut back vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim overhanging branches above the driveway so fire trucks and emergency vehicles can move along the full length of the route without interference.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, leaf litter, and dead plant material that could block or slow vehicle access.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from the brush area closest to the structure.
• Thin shrubs and small trees in the area immediately surrounding the structure to open sightlines and allow movement around the building on all sides.
• Clear vegetation along the single access route consistently, since it is the only way in and out for emergency vehicles.
• Remove any shrubs or tall grass growing in the open terrain areas closest to the structure to reduce the amount of burnable material near the building
